Re: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Jordan Brooks, Member ID W789350798
Reference number: POC-E7809C09B9-10970
Date of notice: 2026-08-03
Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Treating surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement (CPT 27130), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03, reference number POC-E7809C09B9-10970. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in that notice (due by 2027-01-30).

**Stated reason for denial**

The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I dispute this conclusion. The records already in my file — and summarized below — document a substantial, multi-modality, provider-directed course of conservative treatment that lasted approximately 12 months.

**Policy identified as applicable**

I understand this determination was made under Cigna's coverage policy CMM-313: Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty (developed for Cigna by EviCore/Evernorth), the guideline that governs CPT 27130. I was able to independently locate and review a version of this policy dated effective March 7, 2026, which appears to be the version in force on the date of my denial. I want to be transparent about what I could and could not verify directly from that document:

- I was able to confirm the following language verbatim from that policy document:
  - Definition of "Non-Surgical Management": "Non-Surgical Management (with regard to the treatment of lower extremity joint pain) any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain. The types of treatment involved can include, but are not limited to, the following: relative rest/activity modification; weight loss; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non-prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or, intra-articular injections."
  - General Guidelines statement: "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis."
  - From the policy's Tönnis Classification System, used to grade hip osteoarthritis on plain radiographs: "Grade 2: small cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum with moderate joint space narrowing and moderate loss of femoral head sphericity" and "Grade 3: large cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum, severe joint space narrowing or obliteration of the joint space, and severe deformity and loss of femoral head sphericity."
  - From the "Partial Hip Resurfacing Arthroplasty Indications" section of the same policy document, the functional and conservative-care standard used elsewhere in this guideline: "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"; "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"; and "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration."

- I was **not** able to obtain the exact text of the "Total Hip Replacement Indications" section of CMM-313 — the section that specifically applies to CPT 27130 — in the version effective on my date of denial. I am not quoting or attributing any specific total-hip-replacement criteria language to Cigna beyond what is shown above, because I have not verified it. I formally request that Cigna/EviCore provide, as part of this appeal, the complete, specific criteria and citation (section name, version number, and effective date) that the reviewer actually applied to deny CPT 27130 in my case, as required for a full and fair review of an adverse benefit determination.

**How the clinical record addresses "adequate trial of conservative treatment"**

Regardless of the precise total-hip-replacement wording, the plan's own definition of "Non-Surgical Management" (quoted above) and the conservative-care standard applied elsewhere in CMM-313 both point to the same categories of treatment: activity modification, supervised physiotherapy, medications, assistive devices, and intra-articular injections, sustained over a period of months. My record documents all of these categories, sustained well beyond three months:

- **Symptom duration:** 12 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest — this alone exceeds any three-month duration threshold reflected in the policy's parallel provisions.
- **Supervised physiotherapy:** 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait training, 2026-05-01 through 2026-07-10, with 24 completed visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This satisfies the "supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises" component of "Non-Surgical Management."
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, satisfying the "prescription and non-prescription medications" component.
- **Injection therapy:** A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-20, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms recurred, satisfying the "intra-articular injections" component and demonstrating that this modality was tried and failed to provide durable benefit.
- **Assistive device:** The patient currently ambulates with a cane, satisfying the "assistive devices" component and independently demonstrating loss of function.
- **Functional loss:** The patient is limited to walking one block and cannot put on shoes unassisted — this meets and exceeds the "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living" standard quoted above from this same policy.
- **Imaging:** A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-06-25 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes — findings consistent with the severe joint-space narrowing described in the policy's own Tönnis Grade 2–3 definitions quoted above.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion corroborate the imaging and functional findings.
- **No contraindications:** There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and the patient is a non-smoker — none of which present any barrier to surgery.

Taken together, this is a documented, provider-directed, multi-modality conservative treatment course — activity modification, supervised physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection — carried out over approximately 12 months and confirmed to have failed. This directly addresses the stated reason for denial.

**Requested action**

1. Reverse the adverse determination and approve prior authorization for total hip replacement, CPT 27130, for Jordan Brooks; or
2. In the alternative, if Cigna maintains that additional or different criteria under CMM-313's "Total Hip Replacement Indications" section were not met, provide the specific criteria language and citation relied upon so that Dr. Duval's office can respond directly to that specific requirement within this appeal.

**Enclosures**

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-01 to 2026-07-10, 24 visits)
- Medication history documenting 8 months of NSAID use
- Record of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-20 and outcome
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report, dated 2026-06-25
- Office visit/exam notes documenting provocative testing, range of motion, and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Duval, MD
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03 (reference POC-E7809C09B9-10970)

I request written acknowledgment of receipt of this appeal and a decision within the timeframe applicable to a pre-service medical necessity appeal. If this appeal is denied, I intend to pursue my right to independent external review through the Nebraska Department of Insurance under the Health Carrier External Review Act, and I reserve all rights in connection with this claim.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address, phone number, and email listed above.

Sincerely,

Jordan Brooks
